narrative_purpose: Shows Pandora's address from outside: a moon hugging a gas giant that orbits a sun-like star, with the system's two other suns far off in the dark.
subject: A view from deep space. A bright yellow-white star at left. At a distance from it, a banded gas giant planet (cream, rust and grey bands, one large eye-storm), with a small blue-green glowing moon close beside the giant. Far away in the black on the right, two faint distant suns: one small orange point and, much fainter, a tiny dim red point.
scene: The silent dark of interplanetary space, dusted with faint stars. Soft lens-free starlight; the giant planet half-lit by the yellow star, its night side dark. The little moon catches both direct starlight and a faint reflected glow from the giant.
camera: Wide, flat, almost diagrammatic space view from a great distance, everything seen side-on like an orrery laid out across the frame.
light: The yellow star is the key light from the left; gentle rim light on the planet and moon; the two distant suns are faint glints only.
palette: Void-indigo space, a warm yellow-white star, cream-and-rust planet bands, cyan-teal moon glow, one scarce orange and one faint red distant point.
style: Painterly naturalist astronomical plate, soft and atmospheric, NOT a hard vector diagram and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: Moderate: clear shapes and spatial relationships, painterly texture, soft edges; no hard outlines.
composition: Star far left, giant planet and its moon centre, the two faint distant suns far right - reading left to right as a spread-out system, with generous dark negative space.
consistency_notes: Same banded gas giant Polyphemus as the cover. No drawn orbit lines or labels of any kind - this reads as a painted scene, not an annotated chart.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no orbit lines, no arrows, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
